answers.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle 9 Conflict II cards and deal 5 above them; shuffle 3 Conflict I cards and deal 1 on top. This makes a face-down 10-card deck. Return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.

Four-player human: start at 1 VP; three-player human: start at 0 VP. Both start with two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; three troops in their nearest garrison and nine in supply; and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Score marker—on 1 for a four-player game, otherwise on 0”; “two Agents”; “three…garrison…remaining nine”; “Take 1 water.”

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain; after Revealing, your turns are skipped for the rest of Player Turns. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed in the Reveal turn, not cards played on Agent turns. Clean Up moves all cards in front of you (Agent and Reveal turns) to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Reveal turn may be taken early; “Resolve Reveal Effects”; “Clean Up”

answers.answer: No: entry costs must be paid immediately before resolving effects from the destination or the played Agent card, so those later resources cannot pay that entry. One card sends only one Agent, using one chosen Agent icon. A card without Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn; it may be revealed.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Agent Turn entry-cost timing; “You choose only one Agent icon”; “no Agent icons”

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all three troops recruited this turn plus up to two from the garrison: five total in this example. A non-Combat space does not permit normal deployment. Recruits come from your supply into your garrison; at a Combat space, recruited this turn may then deploy.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying Units: “any or all units recruited during your current turn…plus up to two more”

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon permits sending an Agent to a space connected to an observation post where your Spy currently sits; you do not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy at a connected post to bypass another player’s Agent, not your own. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy for one card draw, chosen immediately after Agent placement and before any space/card effects. The same Spy cannot serve both abilities; two different Spies can serve Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, but only one Gather Intelligence draw is allowed per placement.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: “Separate Spy costs and Spy Agent access”; “Gather Intelligence”

answers.answer: Strength is 2 troops × 2 + 1 sandworm × 3 + 4 swords = 11. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. You cannot play Combat Intrigue without at least one unit in the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, sword 1; “if your last unit is ever removed”; Intrigue cards

answers.answer: Yes. Passing earlier does not prevent acting again if an opponent later plays; the window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to each player's supply (not garrison), Combat markers reset to 0, and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: “not required to pass just because you passed earlier”; cleanup

answers.answer: With two tied for first in four-player play, each gets the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward. Nobody wins the Conflict or takes its card. The same tie in a three-player game gives each tied player the second reward, no other reward, and nobody takes the card. A zero-strength player receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: “Exactly two tied first”; “A player with 0 strength receives no reward.”

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards; multiple worms do not multiply beyond doubling. Control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 3 spice to gain 1 VP, you may pay 3 spice once for 1 VP, or pay the cost a second time (6 spice total) to gain 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: “one or more”; exceptions and optional reward example

answers.answer: After winning and taking the Conflict card face up into your supply, check for a match against another face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply. A match is mandatory: flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. In the Endgame, a wild icon may match any one of the three battle icons in your supply, for the same 1 VP pair flip.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: “must flip the matching pair”; Endgame wild match

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses it, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if you fall below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. The first player to 4 also takes the Alliance and its 1 VP. Merely tying the Alliance holder does not steal it: you must rise above their Influence (or the separate FAQ holder-loses-Influence rule may transfer it).
answers.evidence: Scoring: Faction Influence: “At 2 Influence”; “two separate rewards”; “tying…does not steal”

answers.answer: During your Reveal turn, Persuasion may be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool it across sources to buy one card or split one source across cards. After buying a Row card, refill the Row immediately and you may buy the replacement if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Reveal timing, pooling/splitting, Row refill, discard pile

answers.answer: A visit to a Maker space takes all bonus spice there. At Makers, an Agent-free space gets one additional spice during Makers phase. Deep Desert costs 3 water and Hagga Basin costs 1 water. Worm options require Maker Hooks; a protected Conflict at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin cannot receive a summoned worm while the Shield Wall remains. The usual sandworm icon may require Hooks if printed as a condition, but Hooks are not universally required; they are retained, not spent. A sandworm can never go in a garrison, and cannot be summoned at those three protected Conflicts until the Wall is removed.
answers.evidence: Sandworms; Makers; Board Space Guide; Shield Wall

answers.answer: Endgame triggers at the end of a round if any player has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue; then compare VP. Tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: “At the end of a round”; Endgame Intrigue; tiebreakers

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM starts with two face-up contracts and 18 face-down in the bank. Add four CHOAM Imperium cards and four CHOAM Intrigue cards to their respective decks. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back contracts belong to Rise of Ix compatibility and are left out of standard CHOAM.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: Setup changes; “20 standard contracts”; contrasting-back set

answers.answer: With CHOAM, take a face-up public contract and refill its offer face up from the bank if possible; if none are face up, gain 2 Solari. Harvest completes by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the contract’s spice amount that turn in total, including other sources. Immediate completes when taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: Taking contracts; Completing contracts

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a board space where you already sent your Agent this turn, you must wait for a future turn; you must hold the contract when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.

Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. It gets the Ornithopter Objective; humans randomly receive the other two eligible Objectives, and the human with the First Player marker on their Objective goes first. Turn order begins First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival takes Agent turns while it has Agents and never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup; Agent turns

answers.answer: Ignore an occupied destination and reveal another Hagal card; Place Spy cards do not place an Agent, so attempt an empty post of the specified type, then immediately reveal another Hagal card whether placement succeeded or not. Rival ignores ordinary board-space costs/effects and applies only Hagal effects (including its resource, Influence, Signet, troop, Spy and Hooks icons). If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns; Place Spy cards; ignore normal space costs/effects; Reshuffle

answers.answer: Omit Objective cards marked for a different player count, shuffle eligible cards, and give each player one random Objective face up. Its First Player marker identifies the first player. Shaddam may be used only with the CHOAM Module.
answers.evidence: Setup: Objective cards; Shaddam setup restriction

answers.answer: Solari, spice and water tokens and sandworms are not meant to be limited; make convenient substitutions if the bank runs out. An empty personal troop supply means you cannot recruit more until troops return to it. Resource payments go back to the common bank.
answers.evidence: Setup: “These are not meant to be limited”; Recruiting; bank rule

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal the next Conflict, resolve any defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards. If Recall does not trigger Endgame, humans return Agents to Leaders; in 3–4 human play pass First Player clockwise, while in two-player play return Rival Agents to supply and pass First Player to the other human.

Yes, after paying entry costs and meeting requirements first, you may resolve the board-space effects, Agent-box effects and Faction Influence in any order. Therefore the Influence from that visit cannot satisfy that visit’s entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay before effects; “may carry out all these effects in any order.”

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost/effect may be paid only once per turn; do not repeat it to multiply its effect. Most card and space effects are mandatory. Effects marked “may,” arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon are optional; a direct instruction to trash itself is mandatory. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ: Mandatory effects and costs

answers.answer: Place a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have none in supply when placement is needed, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If the placement effect specifies a required connected Agent-icon type, the Spy may be placed only at a post connected to that icon; otherwise placement is not legal.

No: Infiltrate cannot bypass your own Agent. A Spy does not allow an Agent turn without playing a card and meeting its normal icon access condition. No: two Spies cannot be recalled to get two Gather Intelligence draws on one placement; at most one draw is allowed.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Infiltrate; Gather Intelligence; FAQ Spies

answers.answer: At Arrakeen, Spice Refinery and Imperial Basin, the controller gains the location bonus whenever any player visits, including the controller themself. Winning the corresponding Conflict places/replaces a Control marker. If the Conflict is revealed for a location you already control, you may deploy one troop from your supply directly to the Conflict, without an Agent visit. Control may transfer when another player wins that location Conflict.

A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward; the Conflict winner keeps first reward and card, with no further rewards. A tie for third receives nothing. Three tied for first each take second reward; nobody else receives rewards and nobody takes the card.

In an ordinary three-player Conflict with distinct positive strengths, first and second place receive their rewards; third place receives nothing. This is also the reward rule when a two-player game’s Rival is the third competitor.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: player count determines which ranks are paid

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played on your Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues during Combat if you have at least one unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down separate from your deck; after resolving, discard them face up beside the Intrigue Deck. If its draw deck runs out, shuffle its discard into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Intrigue cards; FAQ Draw timing

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction discards a chosen card from your hand and cannot discard an Intrigue unless specified. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes an Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Secrets steals one Intrigue at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigue cards.

Trash effects can remove cards from your hand, discard pile or in play. Return trashed cards to the box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or a card directs you to trash itself. The Spice Must Flow acquire VP remains even if the card is later trashed.

An acquire-box effect resolves once when you acquire that card. If you cannot draw because your deck is empty, reshuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of Reveal and cannot carry over.

Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed on Reveal turns remain in play until Clean Up (unless trashed first). Fremen Bond can use one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards may activate each other regardless of order played. Clean Up ends that in-play status by moving the cards to discard.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: In play / Fremen Bond

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just placed; the recalled Agent may be used on another Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop moves from Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” may mean zero.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ Combat and troops

answers.answer: A free-choice effect granting two Influence requires choosing one Faction for both; it cannot be split. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction’s Alliance token. An effect with a minimum Influence requirement requires that level in the named Faction.

If the holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, and both remain tied, the former holder chooses which tied opponent receives the Alliance. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the token to the board; the former holder loses its VP.

A card drawn during Reveal is revealed immediately and used this turn; a card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, then you draw five additional cards. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect remains face up until then, is used, then discarded.
No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because nobody wins. If received as a reward for an outright win, it may be played immediately.
If VP and all listed resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed 12 spaces.

No. All contracts held for the same space must be fulfilled with one Agent placement; you cannot delay completion. Their effects are another effect of the Agent turn and may resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects, provided you held them when placing the Agent.

Shaddam does not begin with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts; only he may acquire them, choosing one instead of a public contract when acquiring a contract. His Signet restriction begins immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the whole round.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: Reserved Sardaukar; Shaddam; FAQ Shaddam

answers.answer: Feyd’s token begins on the leftmost space of the Training track; when it reaches the rightmost space, it stays there. Lady Jessica begins with her Lady Jessica side face up. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.

Yes, moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2. Margot/Irulan may reach 2 with that Faction again later after losing Influence and regaining it; moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding from hand does.

Accept Contract uses Spice Trade access; it costs nothing, always draws one card, and resolves the contract icon: without CHOAM gain 2 Solari; with CHOAM take a public face-up contract and refill if possible, or gain 2 Solari if offers are exhausted. It gives no automatic Faction Influence and is not Combat. Dutiful Service uses Emperor access, costs nothing, gains one Emperor Influence (counted once) and resolves the same contract icon; it is not Combat. It advances Emperor automatically, unlike Accept Contract.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; human contract icon rule; Faction status

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, controller gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit two troops and draw two cards.

Deep Desert uses Spice Trade access, costs 3 water, and offers either 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms. Hagga Basin also uses Spice Trade, costs 1 water, and offers either 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one sandworm. Both grant all accumulated bonus spice regardless of choosing worms; Hooks are retained, not spent.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; Sandworms; FAQ Spies/Hooks

answers.answer: Both Sietch Tabr options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit one troop, gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second option gives no troop.

High Council uses Landsraad access and costs 5 Solari each visit; it is not Combat. First visit: place Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Subsequent visits: gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue and recruit three troops.

Swordmaster uses Landsraad access; it costs 8 Solari before anyone gains Swordmaster, and 6 once anyone has one. Each player may do it once per game. Take the third Agent, available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival getting its Swordmaster also lowers human cost to 6.

Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access, costs 3 Solari and requires 2+ Emperor Influence; it is not Combat. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence.
Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence and costs 3 spice; it is not Combat. Gain 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction, not necessarily the Guild.

Gather Support uses Landsraad access, is not Combat, and lets you choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari: recruit two troops; if you paid 2 Solari, also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery uses City access and is Combat; choose to pay 0 or 1 spice to gain respectively 2 or 4 Solari; its controller separately gains 1 Solari.

Heighliner: Spacing Guild icon, 5 spice cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Guild Influence and recruit five troops. Desert Tactics: Fremen icon, 1 water cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence, recruit one troop and optionally trash a card. Sardaukar: Emperor icon, 4 spice cost, Combat no; gain 1 Emperor Influence, draw an Intrigue and recruit four troops.

Assembly Hall: Landsraad icon, no cost, not Combat; draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage: Bene Gesserit icon, costs 1 spice, not Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card and place a Spy. Deliver Supplies: Spacing Guild icon, no cost, not Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.

False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent’s destination that turn; it may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear’s red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ: False Orders; Litany Against Fear

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If still unacquired at the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.

Rival starts with four cubes at the bottom of Influence tracks, three troops in garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply with Swordmaster beside board, three Spies, and 1 water in supply; score and Combat marker start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal near the Rival and retain the 2P Reshuffle card. Its 10+ VP triggers Endgame and it can win.

When its total resources reach its printed Swordmaster value, spend exactly that amount and take its third Agent, usable in the current round. Count all Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water in supply, each one counting as one, including starting water. Mandatory spend order: Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, then water; keep leftovers after paying the value. The Agent is immediately usable.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Swordmaster resource total and spending priority

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, spend each exact set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards or 3 water for 1 VP. Mixed resource totals do not qualify; it cannot spend a mixed seven for VP.

Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by leftmost priority icon. It gains VP at 2 Influence and Alliance VP as a human does, but not the 4-Influence track bonus. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means that position in its Rival card’s Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Influence; resource gains

answers.answer: No. For a two-destination card, use only the condition-matching destination; if that destination is occupied, reveal another Hagal card without using the other destination. Conditions are Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping, and Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner.

Yes, at every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops, even if the card recruited none. At a noncombat space recruited troops go into its garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus not met does not prevent Agent placement; just omit that bonus.

Unless specified, choose the first available Faction observation post in priority order. If all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing its third/final supply Spy immediately recalls its other two Spies and triggers Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Spies and Schemes

answers.answer: If Scheme recruits before placement and the Rival visits a Combat space that turn, deploy those newly recruited troops too. If Place Spy finds no empty post of the required type, ignore the placement, then immediately reveal another Hagal card and continue the Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns; Spies and Schemes

answers.answer: The Rival always takes all bonus spice at a visited Maker space. At Hagga Basin/Deep Desert, if it has Hooks and the Conflict permits worms, it summons one/two worms instead of base spice; if it summons none, it takes base spice (2/4). Without Hooks, or if worms are prohibited by the Wall, it takes base spice. Hooks are not spent.

At Combat start, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add only its bottom swords to strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Then humans have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A Rival with no deployed unit gets no bonus.

Yes: Rival gains control, defensive troops, battle-icon VP and sandworm-doubled rewards normally. It always takes optional Conflict VP if it can pay resources or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.

During Reveal effects, total/announce strength and set the Combat marker at any point, updating it as needed. If strength exceeds 20, flip marker to +20 side and start again from the beginning of track.
A human Leader’s Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when revealed. Card text may override usual game rules.

A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for an effect. It does not by itself mean Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those abilities have their own effects and timing.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spies & observation posts; Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence

answers.answer: Trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction instead discards a chosen card from your hand, and cannot be an Intrigue unless specified.

When sandworm doubling applies to a Conflict reward granting 1 Influence, the reward is received twice, and the two gains may go to the same Faction or different Factions. Contrast a single effect granting two free-choice Influence: both must go to one Faction.
Resolve the Signet Ring ability printed on the Rival card, not its Scheme. It is triggered by the Hagal Signet Ring effect; no human Signet Ring card or Rival Reveal turn is involved.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Rival Signet Ring and Scheme

answers.answer: Hagal Maker Hooks takes one token if the Rival lacks Hooks; if it already has Hooks, take none. Shield Wall removal removes the Wall only if Rival has Hooks and Wall remains; without Hooks or when Wall is already gone, ignore it.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Rival Hooks and Wall icons

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, no cost, not Combat. Gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draw an Intrigue from the Intrigue deck; additionally, each opponent with 4+ Intrigues gives one selected at random.

Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, no cost, Combat yes. Visitor gains 1 base spice plus all bonus spice there; controller gains 1 spice. If the visitor controls it, that player receives both visitor gains and controller bonus.

At Round Start, reveal a new Conflict from the top and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any unclaimed Conflict cards from prior rounds; resolve defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards.

Each human places one cube at the bottom of each of the four Faction tracks. Four Alliance tokens start on marked areas of the four tracks; no human starts with one. Shield Wall token begins in its marked area below Spice Refinery.

First Player starts and turns continue clockwise, one turn at a time; a player who Reveals is skipped thereafter. In 3–4 player play, Player Turns ends when all players have Revealed. During Combat Intrigue, First Player starts and priority continues clockwise; each eligible player may play any number or pass, and the window closes after involved players pass consecutively.

Reveal turn: (1) reveal all remaining hand cards; (2) resolve their Reveal box effects, in any order, spend Persuasion and set Combat strength; (3) Clean Up all cards in front of you to discard. Effects need not resolve in card order.

Without CHOAM omit CHOAM-marked cards, shuffle each human 10-card starter and place it face down in supply; shuffle Intrigue and Imperium decks separately, face down; deal five face up to Imperium Row; place Prepare the Way and Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Human Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies, Councilor and three Control markers start in personal supply.
answers.evidence: Setup; Initial card states; Human component layout

answers.answer: During a Reveal turn, spend Persuasion to acquire any of five Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card (Prepare the Way or The Spice Must Flow). Cost is at top right. Ordinary Persuasion purchases are made during Reveal, not Agent turn.

Yes, ordinary human Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even when legal. Shield Wall destruction is optional (“may remove”); once removed it is returned to the box and cannot return later.

Normally the played Agent card needs an Agent icon matching the destination’s access icon, and the space must be unoccupied. A Spy connected to Shipping does not let a City-only card send there. A card with the Spy Agent icon plus a Spy at a connected post does permit access to the connected space without recalling the Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn; Separate Spy costs and Spy Agent access

answers.answer: Yes. You may first play a legal Plot Intrigue before placing the Agent; resources it grants before entry join your available resources and can pay the cost. Resources gained only after placement, from destination or Agent card, cannot pay that same entry.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Plot Intrigue and Agent turn entry costs

answers.answer: No. Even after both humans Reveal, Player Turns continues for the Rival’s remaining Agent turns; skip revealed humans. Combat begins only after both humans have Revealed and Rival has used all its Agents. Rival never Reveals.

answers.evidence: Board Space Guide — Standard 2–4 Players table

answers.answer: A controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict when a Conflict card is revealed for a location already under their control; it is optional and needs no Agent visit. After rewards, all Combat markers reset to 0 before Makers phase.
answers.evidence: Round Start; Critical Locations & Control; Combat cleanup

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching space; resolve that card’s Agent box only. You cannot reuse a card already in play or discard, nor move an Agent already on the board as the turn’s placement.
The restriction applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send the Agent. He cannot postpone it by resolving board space first; recruited troop cannot deploy that turn.

With four different positive strengths and no sandworms, first, second and third ranks each receive their printed reward; fourth receives none. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card, then checks for a battle-icon match.
Players may choose a Leader or select at random; random distribution is not required.
An ordinary draw comes from your own deck. You cannot choose a card directly from discard; if deck is empty, shuffle discard into a new deck and continue.
Shuffle House Hagal and place the deck near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.
All four Maker Hooks begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. A player later acquiring one moves it from the bank onto their garrison.

Yes, adjust Combat marker when a Combat Intrigue changes deployed units or otherwise changes strength, during the Combat Intrigue window. Reveal strength is not fixed; use the adjusted strength shown on the track to resolve Combat.
Gained Solari, spice or water comes from the bank. You do not take it from another player’s supply.
Shuffle the 20 standard contract tokens face down, then flip two face up as offers and leave the rest face down in bank. Players do not choose offers or preset the order.

If Shaddam is chosen, set aside both Sardaukar contracts before the initial shuffle; only Shaddam may acquire them, and he does not start possessing them. Shuffle the remaining 18, expose two face-up offers and leave 16 face down in bank, plus the two reserved contracts.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: Setup changes; Reserved Sardaukar contracts
